So, I was in Prague last summer, and I got this weird vibe when I walked into the train station. Like, I’m in the EU, but somehow I felt like I was in a different world. You know, the way people were speaking, the architecture—it just felt... different.      I know what you mean. I was in Budapest a few months ago, and I got lost in this little back street. There was this old man, like 70, with a beard like a lion, who just started talking to me in Hungarian. I couldn’t understand a word, but he made me feel welcome. That’s the EU for you—total melting pot.      Yeah, but I think the real difference is the way people feel about it. In the UK, we’re always like, “We’re part of Europe, but we’re not really.” Like, we’re on the outside looking in, even though we’re technically still part of it.      I think that’s a bit of a myth. I mean, if you’re a student like me, you’re in and out of the EU every week. You don’t really think about it. You just grab a train, cross the border, and it’s like, “Oh, right, I’m still in the EU.” It’s not something you  think  about, it’s something you  do .      Exactly. And I think that’s what’s so weird about Brexit. Like, people are suddenly hyper-aware of the EU, but they don’t  actually  spend time there. I was in Spain last year for a conference, and I just felt this strange mix of nostalgia and anxiety. Like, “Is this place still safe? Are we still connected?”      I got that. I was in Florence for a week, and I kept thinking, “What if all this changes?” I tried to act normal, but I was just so aware of the borders. You know, I’d always been able to move freely, but now I felt like I was walking on eggshells.      It’s really strange. I think the EU does a lot of good stuff, but it’s not something you notice unless you’re actually living it. I mean, I was in Germany for a few weeks, and I just wanted to say, “This is the real EU.” But I never did. I just went about my day, like, “Okay, I’m here, so I’m good.”

So, I think we’ve decided that we need to take a break from Monopoly... or at least from me trying to win.      Yeah, it’s been going on for ages! I mean, you’ve been trying to buy up all the properties, and now you’ve got the whole board, but you still haven’t got a single penny?      That’s because you’re just building hotels on properties you can’t afford. You’re like the guy in the story who builds a castle on the sand.      Oh, I know, I know. But I still think it’s fun. My kids love watching me try to get out of jail.      I don’t know how you do it. I’m just a kid, and I can’t even remember where I am on the board half the time.      Yeah, I keep getting confused. So, what’s up? You’ve been staring out the window for like five minutes. You alright?      Yeah, I’m fine. Just thinking. You know how it is. Sometimes your mind’s running a mile a minute, and you just need to sit in silence for a bit.      Yeah, I get that. I’ve been thinking about the job offer I got last week. It’s not the biggest deal in the world, but it’s a step up. Didn’t think I’d be getting offers at my age.      Wait, you’re considering it? That’s great! You always said you wanted to be in a more stable role. This could be the thing.      It’s not like I had many options, you know? I’ve been working at the college for three years now. It’s steady, but not exactly challenging. I mean, I like working with people, but I feel like I’m not growing.      I can see that. That was  a  cardboard, and it took me three weeks to get it flying. I was  thisclose  to giving up.      Yeah, but you did it. You always did. Maybe I should start thinking about that job. I guess. It just feels like such a big change. I mean, I’ve worked with the same people for years. It’s not like I’ll be moving to another country or anything.      No, it’s not. But it’s a chance to grow. You’ve got to take risks sometimes, you know?      I know. I just don’t want to make the wrong decision. What if I’m not ready for all that responsibility?      You’ll be ready. You always are. It’s just a matter of when you let yourself believe it. You’ve got this, you know.      Thanks.

Well, I’ve been thinking about the old days, you know. When I was a civil engineer, and I got to see some of the biggest projects in the country. I remember when I was working on that bridge near Norwich. It was a real challenge, but we pulled it off.      That sounds like a fine job, lass. I’ve always fancied myself as a builder, but I never got the chance. I was more of a handyman, you know. Built a few sheds, did a bit of fencing. But nothing like what you did, Jim.      Oh, I know. You were always the sort to get your hands dirty, Phil. You were the type that could fix a boiler or mend a roof. I’ve got to admit, I’m glad I didn’t have to do that sort of thing.      You both are such a pair. I remember when you two used to argue over which was better — concrete or timber. I used to sit there, laughing, while you two got into it like schoolboys.      Oh, come on, Ruth. I wasn’t arguing. I was just stating facts. And you know what, I’ve got a bit of a soft spot for concrete. It’s solid. Reliable.      I’ll say, it’s durable, but it gets cold. You don’t get that with timber. You know what I mean? It’s more forgiving, in a way.      Yes, but it’s not as decorative. I mean, you can’t paint a concrete wall like a timber one. You can make it look all right, but it’s never quite the same.      That’s true, but it’s got its own charm. You know, I’ve been thinking about the old days, the long hours, the hard work. But I suppose it’s all in the past now. I’ve got nothing to do, really.      I know, I know. It’s a bit of a shame. We used to have something to look forward to. Even if it was just a job. But I suppose we’re all in the same boat, aren’t we?      Yeah, it’s tough. But I’ve got the kids, and they’re all right. I’m still busy with the nursery, and the other mums come in and out. It keeps me occupied, even if it’s not what I wanted.      True. I suppose we all have our own way of staying busy.

So, I just wanted to check in on the Honest Skincare business. How's it going? You mentioned you were planning to expand your online presence, right?      Yeah, honestly, it's been a bit of a rollercoaster. We’ve had some great feedback on our products, especially the organic face oils, but we’re still figuring out the best way to market them. I’ve been trying to get more visibility on social media, but it’s not easy. You know how it is—everybody’s got a beauty brand these days.      I know, it's really competitive. But you’ve got a unique selling point—your ingredients are all ethically sourced and cruelty-free. You should definitely leverage that. Maybe create some content around the story behind the products. People love authenticity.      That's what I was thinking too. I was actually planning to do a blog post about our sourcing process. But I’m worried about the time it takes to create content consistently. I’m running a small business, so I can’t afford to be overworked.      I completely get that. Maybe you could outsource some of the content creation? Or use tools like Canva to help with design. I know a few freelancers who do social media management. You could test them out with a small budget first.      That’s a good idea. I’ve been thinking about hiring someone for that. But what about the packaging? I’ve been told that the packaging is a bit generic. Maybe you could suggest some ideas?      Oh, definitely—packaging is key. You should think about eco-friendly materials and maybe even custom labels that reflect the brand’s values. I remember seeing some really creative packaging on Instagram the other week. It’s not just about looking good, it’s about making people feel like they’re part of something bigger.      That’s true. I’ve been thinking about doing a limited edition packaging line for the holiday season. Maybe something with a festive twist but still maintaining the ethical aspect.      That sounds perfect. And you could use that as a way to promote your brand on social media. Maybe create a mini campaign around it. You could even get customers to share their unboxing experiences with a branded hashtag.      I like that. It might help with engagement. I’ll start brainstorming some ideas this week. Thanks for the advice, it’s really helpful.

I’ve been trying to get back into some sort of routine, Claire, but it’s hard when you don’t know where to start. You know, since I retired, I’ve had this feeling like I’ve lost a part of myself. I used to love teaching, you know. It gave me purpose, even if it wasn’t always easy.      I can only imagine, love. I still feel the same way sometimes, even though I’m still working. It’s just different now. I used to have that energy, you know? But I suppose it’s the same for you, isn’t it? You always had a way of making everything seem possible.      You always did, didn’t you? You were the one who used to say, “Even if it’s a difficult class, if you believe in it, you can make it work.” I remember the time when we had that class of troublemakers in Year 11, and you turned it around with a few well-timed jokes and a little bit of flair. It was like magic.      Oh, I had my moments. I still do. I mean, I’ve got that same spark, just not in the classroom anymore. I’ve been thinking about maybe taking on some part-time work, something that’s not too demanding. Maybe tutoring? I’d like to help people out, just like I used to.      That sounds like a good idea. You’ve always had a way with words, you know. Even if you’re not in front of a classroom, your influence still lingers. I think it’s important to keep that going, even if it’s not what you used to do. I’m trying to find something that gives me a sense of purpose again, even if it’s just small things. Like gardening or reading.      That’s a start. You’ve always loved gardening, haven’t you? I remember the time we built that little vegetable patch in the back. It was chaos, but it was also beautiful. Maybe you could start something like that again. You know, growing things, watching them come to life. It’s a quiet kind of satisfaction.      You’re right. I’ve been meaning to get the garden going again. It’s been too long since I’ve had that connection with the earth. I think I’ll start with some herbs. Just a few pots on the windowsill.

So, I just wanted to bring up the heating again. I’ve been trying to get the old system sorted, but the boiler’s been acting up all week. Plus, they can actually help with heating the house more efficiently. I was thinking about it last week, but I’m not sure I want to commit. It’s a bit of a big change. So, I was sorting the cutlery earlier and found this ancient fork that looked like it belonged in a museum. It was so rusty and covered in cobwebs, I thought it was a prop from  The Great Escape  or something.      That sounds like a real find. I was just wondering where the knives had gone—my mum’s kitchen is always a bit of a maze. I swear, half the items are hiding in the back of the cupboard or under the sink.      Oh, I know what you mean. My mum had that  exact  problem. She had this collection of cutlery from every decade, and you’d think she was running a restaurant. I remember one time I was trying to find a butter knife, and I ended up opening the entire drawer—like a scene from a detective movie.      Haha, yeah, I used to do that when I was younger. My mum had this huge set of silverware, and I used to play with it like it was a treasure chest. I think I broke three spoons before I got caught.      You were a menace, Mark. I still remember the time you tried to “rearrange” the cutlery and ended up with a whole set of knives and forks pointing the wrong way. It looked like a war zone.      Oh, that’s my story and I’m sticking to it. I was just trying to make it look more “modern.” But look at it now—my mum’s kitchen is so tidy, I almost feel like I’m in a hotel.      You know, I used to love that sort of thing. When I was a kid, the smell of the kitchen and the way the cutlery clinked when you put it in the drawer—it was like something out of a storybook.      Yeah, I remember that. Even though we didn’t have the best of times, there was something comforting about the routine. My mum always said, “If you keep your cutlery straight, your life will be straight.” I used to think she was just trying to get me to tidy up, but now I think she might have been right.      There’s something about the quiet of a well-kept home. You don’t notice it until it’s gone.      To the cutlery, then. May it always be in order and never rust.      And may we never have to find an ancient fork in the back of the drawer again.

So, I’ve been thinking about our skiing trip, and honestly, I’m starting to feel a bit overwhelmed by all the planning. I’m just worried that I forgot to check the weather forecast for the whole week. What if it’s all slushy and icy? We’ll end up sliding off the slopes like the old man in the ski movie! You even bought those thermal gloves and that waterproof jacket with the fur lining.      Well, it’s not just the gear. I’m also worried about the kids. You know how they get when it’s too crowded. We’re going to play in the snow, eat good food, and maybe even try to teach the kids how to ski. I think it’s a little more than just a holiday to you.      Yeah, I guess you’re right. But you’re the one who signed up for it. I mean, you said you wanted to get out of the house for a while and do something exciting. I think you’re just nervous because you’re not used to being the one in charge.      I suppose you’re right. I just don’t want to ruin the trip for everyone else. I want it to be perfect.      Well, I think you’re going to do great.

Right, so I've been thinking about our Spanish exams. I'm feeling a bit nervous, honestly. I mean, I've been studying pretty hard, but I don't know if I've got everything covered. Maybe we should also talk about our music preferences for a bit? That way, we can take our minds off school stuff.      Yeah, that sounds good. I’ve been really into some indie folk lately. I think I’ve found this band called  The National  – they’re amazing. I’ve been listening to their album  Boxer  non-stop. It’s really emotional, you know?      Oh, I’ve heard of them. I like their music too. I’m more into the electronic stuff – something like  M83  or  Lana Del Rey . Their songs are so atmospheric. Do you think we should start a music playlist together?      That’s a great idea. I’d love that. I mean, it’s not like we can really go out to concerts right now anyway. So maybe we can just listen to our favorite songs and share recommendations. It could be a fun way to relax after school.      Yeah, I think that’s a great plan.

Oh, I just watched  The Favourite  again, and I was so  bitten  by it. You know, that bit where Abigail’s got the earl by the throat? It’s just so  sharp , isn’t it? I mean, the way it’s directed—like, it’s got this real knife-edged feel to it.      I saw it too, but I didn’t get half of it. I mean, it’s got all these political plots and the dialogue is so dense. I had to look up half the names of the characters to even get through it. But I still thought it was  sharp —I mean, in a different way. Like, the way they portrayed the power dynamics, you know? It made me think about how women have always had to play games to get ahead.      Yeah, and the casting was just  beyond  brilliant. Olivia Colman’s performance was so subtle, wasn’t it? She says so little, but you can  read  the whole story just from her expression. I mean, the way she plays with the king—like, she’s got this  villainous  charm, but you can’t quite blame her. She’s just surviving, isn’t she?      She’s the  real  villain, though. You can’t really  sympathize  with her. She’s just manipulating everyone. But then again, the king’s not exactly innocent either. He’s been around a while—what’s he done? He’s just been  bored , isn’t he?      Exactly! I mean, he’s the one who’s  craving  a little chaos. He’s got that sort of king who’s worn out by all the etiquette and the rules. You know, the kind of man who’d much rather have a bit of drama than a boring court.      I think that’s what makes the film so good—how it doesn’t take sides. It’s just  real . It doesn’t paint the characters as good or bad, just  human . I mean, like, the queen is so goody-two-shoes, but she’s not perfect either. She makes mistakes, and she’s just as complicated as the others.      Yeah, that’s it. It’s like a courtroom drama, but with royal intrigue. You can’t help but be drawn in, even if you don’t fully understand the politics. I’m gonna have to watch it again, maybe with some notes, just so I can  get  it.

Well, I've been thinking about that trip to Cornwall we talked about last week. It's been ages since we went on a proper holiday, hasn't it?      Yes, it has. I've been meaning to ask you — do you think you're finally ready to take the plunge and get that car we've been eyeing up? The one with the automatic gear?      Oh, I'd love to, but I'm still not sure. I keep telling myself I'll get around to it, but then the weather turns, or I get caught up with work, or the kids are on holiday. It's like a never-ending cycle.      I know the feeling. You're not the only one who procrastinates like that. But I was thinking, with the way the roads are getting worse in Birmingham, and the weather... ever so unpredictable, maybe you should consider it.      You're right, the roads have been a nightmare lately. And with the kids all off to uni, I’ve got more free time now. But I’m worried about the cost. I know the car’s not cheap.      I hear you. It's a big decision. But think about the long-term savings. Fuel efficiency, insurance, all that. And with the way petrol prices are going, it might be worth it.      I suppose. It’s just that I’ve always been a bit wary of big purchases. I mean, I’ve saved up for a while now, but I keep thinking, "What if things change?"      I understand. You’re not the only one who feels that way. But sometimes you have to take the plunge. You know, the older you get, the less time you have to wait for the perfect moment.      That’s a good point. I’ve been a little too cautious lately. Maybe I should start looking at some options. You know, do a bit of research, see what's on the market.      That’s the spirit! You’ll be glad you did. And if you need any help, I’m always here.      Thanks, Mum. You’re a lifesaver. I think I’ll start doing some research this weekend.      Just make sure you don’t end up buying something you don’t need. And no, definitely no red car.      Oh, you’re still on that, are you?      Absolutely. That red car? Not for you. Not for me.

I still can’t get over how different the sky looks here. It’s almost like the weather is trying to tell us something.      Yeah, I know what you mean. I think it’s trying to say, “Don’t forget to bring an umbrella.” But I reckon it’s not going to rain for a while.      Maybe. But you know what I meant. It’s just so vivid. Back in Norwich, the sky feels more… muted. Like it’s holding its breath.      I’ve noticed that too. You know, I think it’s the altitude. Or maybe it’s the pollution. I don’t know. But I do love how the light here hits the buildings differently.      Yeah, I’ve been thinking about that. The way the light reflects off the glass in the shopping mall we passed earlier. It was like a stained-glass window—so vivid, so colorful.      Right, that’s the one. And the way the light hits the shop windows—it’s almost like the city is dressed up. You ever notice how the reflections make everything seem more… vivid?      Exactly. I did a presentation on urban visual culture last term, and I think that’s what I should’ve included.      Oh, don’t start. You’d have had to explain it to a bunch of students who didn’t even know what  stained glass  was.      I’d have found a way. But seriously, I think this city has a way of making you more aware of the details. Maybe that’s why I feel like I’ve been processing things differently lately.      I get that. Work’s been a bit intense, and I think the change of scenery has helped. Plus, we’ve been shopping more.      Yeah, I’ve been wanting to get some new books for my course. The library’s been so busy, and I need to get some more academic material.      You know what I’ve been thinking about? Maybe we could go to the market tomorrow. The one near the station. I heard they have some good local books and stationery.      That sounds perfect. I’d love to go. You know I love that kind of shopping. It’s so different from the big chain stores.      Yeah, it’s like being in a little world of its own. And it’s much better for the environment, too. Less plastic. Less waste.      I’ll take that as a compliment.

So, I’ve been thinking about the weekend – you know, with the kids. I got the kids sorted for the afternoons, but I still need someone to watch them on Saturday. I was wondering if we could swap babysitting duties?      Yeah, I was thinking the same. I was going to ask if you wanted to take them on Saturday. I’ve got a friend coming over to do a photoshoot, so I’d rather not have the kids around. But I can’t just leave them alone. Didn’t you say you had a friend who’s a babysitter?      Oh, I know someone who’s great. Her name’s Liza. She’s a student, and she’s been helping out with the neighbor’s kids. She’s reliable and I think she’d be happy to take them for a few hours. I can get her details for you.      Can I play with my toys? I want to play with the dinosaur!      Of course, sweetheart, but we need to finish our plans first. What did you say you were doing on Saturday? You were going to see your friend, weren’t you?      Yeah, I’m meeting Emma and her sister for coffee and then we’re going to the park. It’s been ages since we’ve all caught up.      I hope it’s not too far. I don’t want to inconvenience you. I can always take them to the park with me if you want.      No, no, I’m fine. Liza can manage. She’s had kids before. And I’ve already told her about the photoshoot. I think she’s excited about it. She’s been trying to get a local gig for a while.      Can I go to the park too? I want to ride my bike!      Well, if Liza’s watching, you’ll be fine. But maybe you can ride your bike when you’re with her. I’m sure she’ll let you.      Oh, and I was thinking about the dinner. I’ve got this new recipe I found – it’s a baked potato with some homemade pesto. I’ve been reading about it in that cookbook you gave me.      Oh, that sounds lovely. I love pesto. I’m always making my own. You know, I think the kids would like that too. It’s a bit different than the usual chicken and chips.      Yeah, it’s a bit adventurous.

So, I was just telling my mates about the time I tried to order a  proper  burger at that new café near the library, and I ended up with a sandwich that looked like it had been assembled by a robot.      Oh yeah? What happened? Did it come with a side of confusion?      Oh, it came with  so  much confusion. I said, “I want a burger, not a salad,” and the guy just stared at me like I’d asked for a  pretzel  instead of a burger.      That’s not even fair. You should’ve just said, “I want a burger like the one you served me last week.”      Yeah, but I was being  so  proper. You’re telling me you tried to be  vague ?      I was being  specific . I thought I was being a good customer, but apparently, I just confused the poor guy. Always. I’m surviving, but I’m not  thriving . I had to miss a lecture yesterday because I was too busy arguing with a vending machine about whether it was a  refreshment  or a  food  machine.      Are you serious? You’re giving those machines more respect than some people give their lecturers.      I’m trying to be polite. I’ve told them, “Please, just give me a proper snack, not this sad snack.”      I feel you. I once tried to order a  proper  coffee at the canteen, and they gave me what looked like a cup of tea with a tiny bit of foam on top.      Oh, we’re in the same boat. I think we should start a petition for better food at uni. I’m not going to die from a burger that looks like it was made by a robot.      Yeah, but maybe you should just go out and get something real. You know, like a real burger, a real coffee.      Maybe. But I’m not sure I can handle the  responsibility . I might end up needing a therapist.      Then you’ve got me. I’m your food therapist.

So, I was just telling my mates about the holiday I had in Cornwall last summer... It was supposed to be a relaxing weekend, just me and my nan, but we ended up getting stuck in a queue for two hours just to get into a café. The weather was foul, and the place looked like it hadn’t been updated since the '80s.      That sounds like a real winner! I had a similar experience when I was in Somerset a few years back. I was trying to find a decent fish and chip shop, and I ended up walking for like half an hour just to get to one that wasn’t closed. I think the locals had some kind of secret society to keep tourists away from their best bites.      You know, I actually had a good time in Cornwall. I was there for a work trip, but I managed to squeeze in a bit of sightseeing. I went to St Michael’s Mount, and it was amazing. The views were absolutely stunning. But I’ll be honest, I did miss proper English food. Nothing beats a good pint of ale and a full English breakfast.      Yeah, I can see that. I tried a few of the local dishes, but honestly, the fish was a bit too fishy and the chips were more like something you’d find in a takeaway. I think I’ll stick to my usual go-to spots back home.      That’s the thing with holidays, though. It’s all about the experience. Even if the food is a bit off, you’re still in a different place, right? I remember when I was in Germany last year, I tried the sausages and the pretzels, and they were absolutely delicious. It’s just that the weather was a bit of a mood killer.      There’s something about being somewhere new, even if it’s not the best. It’s the stories you take home. I tried to make some friends on the trip, and one of them showed me a local pub that had the best ale in the area. It was worth the trip just for that.      I guess that’s the thing. It’s not just about the food or the weather; it’s about the people and the moments you make. I’ve got a few friends who are planning a trip to Cornwall next year, and I’m looking forward to it.

So, I was thinkin’ the other day, me and Mavis, we’d got to go to London again. I’m gettin’ so tired of the same old places, and I reckin it’s time we went somewhere different. You know, like the place in Southwark? That place with the bridge?      Oh yes, I remember that. A real fine place, though I’ve never got to go there. I’ve always fancied that bridge. You know, the one where they used to chase the horses? Funny how things change, though. I mean, I used to go there when I was a kid, and now it’s all bits of that old town, you know?      You mean the one with the horses? I’ve heard stories about that. They used to keep them in the old stables, and people would go and watch them. It was like a fairground. I remember the day when one of the horses got loose and ran through the street. Made quite a scene.      Oh, I remember that too! You couldn’t get a seat for miles, and the kids were in a right state. But it was a good laugh. You know, I’ve been thinking of taking the car down to Cornwall again. That youth hostel we stayed at last time was amazing. We even met a few people who were looking to sell their houses. Said they wanted to move down south.      Yeah, I heard about that. Some people were looking to sell their cars and houses and go down there. I’ve always fancied a place by the sea, you know. Maybe I’ll look into the houses again. I’ve had a few ideas. Maybe even take the old van down to eBay and see if I can sell a few things. My sister’s got a few bits of furniture she wants to get rid of.      That’s a good idea. I’ve been on eBay myself. Got a few bits of stuff. I even sold a few old books. You’d be surprised how much you can do with a bit of work. Though I still think the best way to make some money is to go to a yard sale or something like that.      I suppose. But I’ve got this idea of buying a house. It’s all so confusing, though. You think you’ve got the money, but then you find out there’s all sorts of fees and taxes and stuff.

So, I just got an email from the midwife about the feeding schedule for the baby. She said it’s important to be consistent with breastfeeding or formula, but also to be flexible if the baby is fussy. I’m trying not to overthink it, but honestly, I’m so nervous about getting it right.      Oh, I get that. I’ve been reading all these articles online about how every baby is different. One said that some babies don’t want to eat every three hours, and others just want to nurse all the time. It’s so confusing.      Yeah, I’ve been trying to make a chart, like a baby feeding log, but then I think, “What if the baby just doesn’t want to eat at the time I’ve planned?” I’m terrified I’ll mess it up.      I know, I was like that too. But honestly, it’s not like you’re wrong if the baby doesn’t want to eat. You’re just not in control, and that’s okay. I mean, I remember when I had my first baby, I thought I had it all figured out, and then the baby would just start crying and I’d be like, “What’s going on?”      That sounds familiar. I’m also thinking about how my mum helped me with the baby’s routine. She used to say, “It’s not about making them do what you want, it’s about meeting their needs.” But I still feel like I’m failing.      You’re not failing. You’re doing the best you can, and that’s all you can do. I think part of the problem is that we’re so used to planning everything. But with a baby, it’s all about being responsive, not rigid.      I guess that makes sense. I just feel like I should be able to figure it out. I mean, I was in graduate school, I can handle anything, right?      Wait, you were in graduate school? That’s amazing! I still can’t believe you were studying something so academically intense.      Yeah, I was doing language research. It was really interesting, but I’m glad I’m done with that. I think I needed a break.      You’re going to be a great mum. I mean, you’re smart, you’re caring, and you’ve got that big heart. You’re going to be amazing.

Right, I’ve been meaning to talk about the garden. The roses are looking a bit lacklustre after the recent rain. I think I need to trim them back a bit, or maybe even replant some. I’ve been meaning to get some new plants for the corner by the shed.      Yeah, I’ve been thinking the same thing. The roses are starting to look a bit straggly. Oh, and the ivy’s getting out of hand again. I was going to tackle that this weekend, but with the weather being so unpredictable, I’m not sure if I’ll get the chance.      I’ve been meaning to get some native plants for the back garden. My mum says they’re easier to care for and attract more wildlife. But I’m not sure about the maintenance. Do you think it’s worth it?      I think it is! I’ve seen some lovely native plants in the local park. They don’t need as much watering, and they’re better for the environment. I’m planning to plant some foxgloves and daffodils next spring.      Foxgloves, eh? I remember when I was a kid, we used to collect those.
