I can’t imagine how you managed to keep track of all those children. I mean, I barely remember my own class schedule.      Oh, it wasn’t all that hard. You just had to be someone they trusted. And also, you had to be a bit of a storyteller. You see, the children would follow you anywhere if you had a good story. I used to tell them about the old castle in the village—how it was built by a man who had a lot of money and a terrible temper.      Sounds like you had your work cut out for you. I used to work with kids in the workshops. They were a handful, but they always had a way of making things interesting. I remember one lad who could stick a nail in a board with one hand while holding a cup of tea in the other.      That’s something I’d love to see. I mean, I work with words, not tools, but I can imagine how much patience it takes to work with people like that.      It’s all about understanding people, isn’t it? Whether it’s children or colleagues, you just have to find the right way to connect with them.

So, I was just thinking, do you two know what the best present I could ever get for Mother’s Day would be? It’s not a gift, it’s a  day  where I don’t have to do  anything  except sit on the couch with a cup of tea and a biscuit.      You’d be so lazy, Mummy! I’d never let you do that!      Yeah, you’d just lie there and eat all the cake!      Exactly! But, of course, I can’t have that. I’ve got to do  something . So, what’s the plan? I was thinking about taking you both to Forest School this weekend. It’s been a while, and I think it would be a nice way to spend some quality time together.      Forest School? Can we go  now ?      No, no, no—this is  next  weekend. But I’m telling you, it’s going to be great. You’ll get to play, get dirty, and probably get a little muddy.      I like getting muddy! I can make a mud pie!      That’s the spirit! You know what else? I’ve heard that Forest School teaches all sorts of things—like how to build a shelter or read the weather. It’s like a real life lesson, but with more sticks and less homework.      Are you saying we’re going to learn  stick  stuff?      Maybe. Maybe not. But I think it’ll be fun. And besides, it’s a chance for us to be outside, which is always better than being inside with a screen.      But what if it rains? Then we can’t go.      Well, if it rains, we’ll just have to find another way to be creative. Maybe we can do something  inside —like a craft project or go to the park. But if it’s sunny, then Forest School is the way to go.      I like that. It’s like a  weather  plan.      Exactly! You’ve got a good brain, you know. You’re already using idioms like  weather  and  plan .      Is that an idiom?      Sort of. It’s like saying “no matter what happens, we’ve got a plan.” It’s a bit of a saying, but it’s a good one.      So, like “when the going gets tough, the tough get going”?      That’s a  real  idiom. Women, you’re getting clever!      I think I’ll call it  The Forest School Plan !

So, I just got a call from the doctor — it’s about the auntie, you know? She’s got cancer again, and it’s not looking good. I can’t even begin to imagine how she’s coping.      Oh no, what a shock. I’m so sorry to hear that. I can’t believe it’s come to this again. How is she holding up? You know how she’s always been so strong.      She’s trying, honestly. She’s got that same stubbornness she had when she was running her own business. But the kids are really worried. They’re all back in town now, helping out. I think it’s been a long time since they’ve all been together like that.      That’s a shame. I know how much she meant to them, and how much they all adored her. It must be so hard for them. I can’t imagine losing someone I love like that. You know, I’ve been thinking about my own mum lately, you know? She’s been through a lot with her heart, and I worry about her, but she’s always been so resilient.      I know. It’s funny how we all have these moments where we feel like we’re not quite in control of our health. I remember when I was younger, I thought I was invincible. But now, I just try to stay in the moment as much as I can. It’s not always easy, especially when you’re watching people you care about struggle.      Yeah, it really does make you stop and think. I had a conversation with my sister the other day about mental health. She’s been under a lot of pressure at work, and she’s been feeling really down. I told her that it’s okay to not be okay, and that she doesn’t have to carry everything on her own. It’s something I’ve learned, you know?      That’s such a good point. I think we all need to be more open about our struggles. I’ve started talking more to my daughter about what she’s going through at school. It’s not always easy, but it’s better than keeping it all inside.      Exactly. I think that’s what makes people like us so strong — the ability to support each other through tough times. And even though it’s hard, I think that’s what we’re here for.

So, I just got back from my morning run, and I was thinking—do you ever get that feeling when you’re out and about, and you just  know  you need to try something? Like, this little café down the road has this Korean flatbread with kimchi, and I just  knew  I had to try it.      Oh, I know! I heard about it from my flatmate, and I’ve been dying to go. But honestly, I’m not sure if I should. I’ve been trying to be more careful with my diet, but the thought of spicy food... I’m not sure if I’m ready.      Yeah, I get that. But you know, I’ve been living in South Korea for a while now, and I’ve learned that their food is  so  different. It’s not just spicy—it’s full of flavor. And honestly, I think you’d love it.      I’d love to, but I’m also thinking about the tuition fees. I mean, I’m still on that student loan, and I don’t want to spend too much. I mean, we’re not even sure if we’ll get the full grant.      I know. I’ve been thinking about that too. But actually, it’s not that expensive, and sometimes they have deals if you buy the whole meal. It’s not like you’re paying for a full course. Plus, it’s been a while since we’ve had anything different.      That’s true. I’ve been cooking a lot lately, but I’m not into the whole vegetarian thing—though I do try to be more conscious. I mean, I’m not vegan or anything, but I do eat less meat.      Yeah, I’ve been doing that too. I mean, it’s not like I’m cutting out meat entirely, but I’ve been trying to balance it out. I’ve been making more veggie dishes, and it’s actually been a nice change.      I think I’m going to try that café this weekend. Maybe with you?      That’d be great. I’ll even bring some cash for the extra bits. I mean, we can go early, get the best seats, and maybe even try one of those Korean fried chicken things they have.      You’re on. I’m actually really excited. I’ve been reading about their festivals, too. Like, the lantern festivals and all that.

So, I just got back from Sugarhouse and it was  mad ! We were all dancing and then this guy in a vest came up and said, “You look like you’ve been doing maths all night.” I was like, “You bet I have—my brain’s in a spin!”      Oh, I know that feeling. I was in the middle of a physics problem and then this guy asked me if I’d like a drink. I said, “No, I’m doing a calculation on the spot.” He said, “Oh, you’re like Jack Whitehall.” I was like, “No, I’m like…  entirely different .”      I’m not sure if I’m laughing or crying. I feel like I’ve been here for  years , but I’m still not over the fact that I once tried to explain  Chaos Walking  to someone in a café and they said, “Is that like,  The Twilight Zone ?”      Yeah, I had that too. I tried to explain it to my flatmate, and she said, “Is it like  The Vampire Diaries  but with extra silence?” I was like, “No, it’s like  The Twilight Zone  but with aliens and  Wayne’s World  vibes.” It was  so  awkward.      I remember when someone said, “Oh, you’re into  Twilight ?” and I had to explain that I had  read  it, and then  read  the  Chaos Walking  trilogy, and then  read   City of Bones  and  The Vampire Diaries  and  How I Met Your Mother  and  The Big Fat Quiz  and I was like, “I’m not just into books, I’m into  everything .”      You’re like a library on legs! I’ve tried to read  Cloud Atlas  but honestly, I lost half of it. I think I read the first part and then just…  zoned out .      I had the same with  University Challenge . I watched one episode and then I was like, “I don’t even know what this is.” I think I’ve seen three minutes of it and already feel like I’ve aged ten years.      Maybe we should start a group quiz. I’ve got  Articulate  and  Heads Up  and  Hungry Hippos . We could do a  Secret Santa  where we have to guess what the other person’s present is. Last year someone gave me a  flavoured vodka  and it was  so  bad. I felt like I was drinking a  triple espresso  with a  Marmite  twist.      I had a  timetable  that was so bad, I accidentally got stuck in a  module assessment  on a Tuesday.

So, I was just thinking about that time we tried to get the bus from Sunderland to Newcastle and ended up getting stuck in this roadworks for like an hour. I nearly lost my mind. I was just about to start shouting at the driver when you pulled up beside me in your car. I swear, I thought I was gonna die.      Yeah, I remember that. You were so worked up, I nearly got pulled over for being too distracted. But I couldn’t just leave you there, could I? Besides, I knew you’d be alright once you got a bit of fresh air. Though honestly, I still don’t know why we didn’t just take the train like everyone else.      Oh, come on, you know what the trains are like. I think the last time I got on one, they nearly dropped me off in a different town. And I was in a hurry to get to the café for that meeting. I was so stressed, I nearly forgot my laptop in the bus stop.      You always were a bit of a mess when you’re flustered. But look at you now, running a corpus like it’s nothing. I mean, I still can’t believe you landed that job at the university. You’re not even a graduate, really—just a degree. I mean, don’t get me wrong, you’ve earned it, but still.      Oh, please. I’ve got a master’s, thank you very much. And it’s not like I got it in a flash. I worked my way up from the bottom, and now I’m in charge of managing all these texts and transcripts. It’s not all cups of tea and tea breaks, you know.      Yeah, I know. You’ve always been good at your stuff. Just… a bit more dramatic about it than I’d like. But I’ll say this—when it comes to work, you don’t mess around. You stick to it like glue.      And you, mate, still whizzing around the country like you’re on some kind of mission. I swear, sometimes I think you go out of your way to be busy. If I had half your energy, I’d be out there doing something exciting instead of sitting in a car waiting for the bus.      You’d be surprised. I’ve got a few projects coming up.

Aye, it's been a bit of a wet start to the week, hasn't it? Blows like a Norf’k gale, and the sun's only just showed its face again. I swear, if it keeps up like this, I'll be stuck indoors all week with the flu.      Aye, I know what you mean. I’ve been feeling a bit under the weather myself. Headache and sore throat, like I’ve been through a battle. I thought it was just the cold, but I reckon it's that damp air. I've been keeping the fire going, but it's like the damp’s still creeping in.      I’m not sure I’d call that a battle. You’re both making it sound like a war. I’ve been out and about this week, and it’s been fine. Though I do miss the warmth of the sun, even if it’s only a few hours a day.      Yeah, listen, I’ve been keeping an eye on the weather forecast. It’s supposed to get better by the weekend, but for now, we’re stuck with this grey drizzle. I’ve even been thinking about getting a new kettle, you know, something that’s more efficient. The old one’s been making a funny noise lately.      Aye, the kettle’s been suspicious for a while. I tried to fix it, but I reckon it’s best to just replace it. I’ve been looking at some new models online, but honestly, I can’t tell the difference. One day it’s a whisper, the next it’s a scream.      I’d say it’s a classic case of a kettle with a ‘personality.’ I’ve got one like that too. It’s been with me since the days when I was a childminder, and it’s been through thick and thin. I think it’s almost like it’s got a soul.      I think the kettle’s just trying to get attention. You know, like the old folks in the village. You get them talking about their cups of tea and the weather, and before you know it, they’ve done a full story on the day.      I think we’re all just trying to make the best of what we’ve got. The weather’s been a bit of a downer, but it’s not all bad. You know, I’ve been thinking about taking up football again.

So, I just got an invitation to my cousin’s wedding. It’s in London next month. I was thinking, should I go? I mean, I haven’t seen her in ages, but I don’t want to be the only one who’s not in a relationship.      Wait, you’re not single? I thought you were dating that guy from the office.      Oh, that’s right. He’s been super busy with his new project. We’ve barely had time to go out. I guess it’s just one of those things. But I still feel like I’m missing out.      I get it. I’m in the same boat. I’ve been seeing this guy for a few months, but we’re both working crazy hours. I’m not sure if we’re even going to make it to the next step.      Yeah, I know what you mean. I’ve been thinking about my ex a lot lately. I mean, not in a bad way, just kind of wondering if I made the right choice. Sometimes I feel like I should have taken the leap earlier.      You know, I think it’s okay to take your time. I mean, I’ve been in a relationship for a while now, but I still have moments where I wonder if I’m making the right decision. It’s not like you’re supposed to have everything figured out at 26.      True. I just feel like everyone else is moving forward, and I’m stuck in this limbo. I mean, what if I miss out on something? What if I’m not ready for marriage?      I think about that a lot too. My parents are really pushy about kids and marriage. It’s like, “When are you going to settle down?” But I’m not in a rush. I just want to be happy.      I think that’s the most important thing. I mean, if you’re not happy, it doesn’t matter how many kids you have or how big your house is. You have to be in a place where you feel good about your choices.      Exactly. I think the key is not to compare yourself to others. Everyone’s journey is different. I mean, I’m engaged, but I’m still figuring out what that means for me.      Okay, fair. So maybe I should just go to the wedding and see what happens.

Aye, it's a real shame about the weather, isn't it? Been a bit of a damp sod all week.      Yes, it's been a bit of a drizzle, hasn't it? I was just thinking about the last time we had proper sunshine. Must have been about three years ago.      That was the year you tried to teach me how to use a mobile phone, and I nearly set the whole thing on fire. Remember that?      Aye, that was the day! You were trying to send a text and you accidentally pressed the camera button. I thought you were taking a photo of the cat, but it turned out you’d just set the whole thing off.      And then you tried to blame it on the cat! I swear, if you ever looked at that thing, you’d have seen the camera button.      Well, I suppose it was a learning curve. Back then, I didn’t even know what a touchscreen was. I used to think it was some kind of wizardry.      Aye, and I used to think the internet was a place where you could actually find things. Now it's just a load of nonsense and cat videos.      I remember when you first got your computer. You thought it was a toaster with a keyboard.      I did! I thought it was a way to make toast with pictures. I even tried to put a picture of a sandwich on it.      I remember that. You were so proud of yourself. But I suppose it was a good start.      You know, I was thinking about the kids. I haven't seen them in ages. They all have their own devices and they're always on their phones.      It's a shame, really. I used to run a school, and I could see how much the kids were getting distracted. It's not just the phones, though. It's the whole world now.      Aye, and with the money problems, it's hard to keep up. I mean, even the postman asks if we want to pay for something online.      I know. I was thinking about taking up something. Maybe gardening, or something like that.      You could always try looking after horses. I know a few people who have horses and they need help.      Not sure. I’ve always been more of a cat person. Though I suppose if it’s for money, I could try.

You know, I’ve been thinking a lot about how language changes. It’s fascinating how people from different regions develop such distinct ways of speaking. I've been teaching English for years, and I still find it amazing how even within England, accents and dialects can make such a difference.      I reckon you'd say that. You're a language teacher, after all. I've always thought that the way people speak is like a fingerprint—every person has their own. I was brought up in Essex, and even though I've lived in Birmingham for a good part of my life, I still can't shake that accent. It’s like a part of me.      That’s interesting. I think it’s not just about accents, though. It’s about the way people use words, the cadence, the rhythm. I’ve noticed that people from the South often use more formal speech, while those from the North tend to be more direct. It's amazing how you can tell where someone's from just by listening.      Absolutely. I remember when I was a managing director, I used to have a lot of meetings with people from different parts of the country. It was sometimes a bit of a struggle getting everyone on the same page. You see, they'd use different terms, and sometimes it just led to confusion. Though, honestly, I think that’s what made it exciting. It taught me to listen more carefully.      That’s a good point. I’ve often told my students that language is not just about grammar and vocabulary—it's about communication. Whether you're from here or there, the goal is to get your message across clearly.      I couldn’t agree more. And speaking of communication, I’ve been meaning to ask you—you know that weekend you mentioned? Are you still planning to go to that festival in the countryside?      Yes, I am. It’s supposed to be a great event. I was thinking about bringing some of the students along too. You know, give them a chance to experience real-life English in action.      That sounds like a good idea. I might just join you. Though I’ll probably bring my tumbler of tea and a goody bag of snacks. I’ve always had a knack for making sure I’m not the only one who’s had a good time.

So, what do you think about this year’s Valentine’s Day? I mean, honestly, I didn’t even have a proper date. Just my flatmate and me, eating takeaway and watching  Tenet  again. No, not that again! I think I’ve watched it like three times now.      Oh, I know! I heard you guys were debating whether it was actually a movie or just a bunch of explosions with confusing time loops. Honestly, I think you’re the only person who actually tried to understand it. Most of the blokes I know just said, “It’s brilliant, I loved it, even though I didn’t get half of it.”      Yeah, and I’m the only one who didn’t get half of it, but I still think it’s amazing. Anyway, I was just thinking—shouldn’t we be out doing something? I mean, it’s Friday, right? People usually go out, eat, watch a movie, or go to a restaurant. I feel like I’ve missed out.      I know, I know! I’ve been trying to get my flatmate to go out, but she’s been stuck in a meeting all week. So I’m stuck here with my mates, just trying to figure out what to do tonight. I was thinking of going to the cinema, but I don’t know what to watch. You know that new horror movie that came out? The one with the guy who gets his face cut off? I thought it was a bit much, but I guess it’s a bit of a trend now.      Oh, I’ve heard about that one! I think it’s called  The Skin  or something like that. I mean, that’s not even a real title, but it sounds way too edgy for me. I’d rather go to a comedy. I was thinking maybe  The Marvels ? Or maybe something from the 80s? I’m in the mood for a classic.      That’s a good idea. I think I’ll go with that. Anyway, I was just trying to figure out what to do with the weekend. I go out on Fridays usually, but this week I’ve been too busy with coursework. I think I’m going to take the weekend off and just relax. Maybe go shopping? I need new clothes, honestly.      Shopping? You? I thought you were the type to just wear the same old jeans and a hoodie all week.

So, I just got my first major project approved — a mixed-use development in East London. It’s going to be residential and some retail spaces. I’m really excited about it, but honestly, the planning process was a nightmare. So much red tape, and the local council is so resistant to anything that doesn’t fit their idea of “traditional” architecture. I feel like I’m fighting against the system every day.      I can only imagine. I’ve been working on a piece about housing inequality in London, and it’s crazy how the system is set up to exclude people who don’t have the right connections or the financial means. I mean, even if you’re a qualified architect, like you, it’s still like climbing a mountain just to get your plans approved.      Exactly. And it’s not just about the planning. I think the whole housing crisis is a symptom of a bigger problem — capitalism. It’s all about profit, not people. You can’t even afford a flat in London anymore, let alone build one. It’s so frustrating.      It’s not just London, you know. I’ve seen it in other cities too — even cities that aren’t as expensive. It’s like the system is designed to keep people in a cycle of debt and displacement. I’ve been thinking about writing something about how the housing market is actually a form of systemic racism. People of colour are often the ones being priced out, or forced into poorer areas with fewer amenities.      That’s not just an opinion — it’s a fact. I’ve noticed that in some of the areas I’ve worked on, there’s a real divide between the wealthy communities and the rest. It’s not just about income, it’s about who gets the resources and the attention. And it’s not just in London either. It’s everywhere.      Yeah, it’s everywhere. I mean, I’m not saying it’s the same everywhere, but the patterns are similar. And it’s not just about housing — it’s about access to education, healthcare, even employment. The system is built to keep people down.      I hate to say it, but I think the only way to change it is to start from the top. If we can get more people in power who understand the real issues — not just the ones that make headlines — maybe we can start making a real difference.

You know, I’ve been thinking a lot about the nursery lately. I feel like I’m not ready to go back to work yet, but I know I have to. It’s just… worrying about the baby being away from me so much.      I can totally understand. It’s so hard to think about leaving them for the first time. I’ve been helping out with the morning routine too, but it’s still a big adjustment. I mean, it’s one thing to be there all day, and another when you’re not.      Exactly. And then there’s the weaning. Have you started yet? I know it’s supposed to be easier, but I’m not sure I’m ready. It feels like such a big change, you know?      Oh, it’s not easy at all. I’ve been trying to introduce solids for a few weeks now, but she’s still pretty stubborn. I thought she’d be more interested in the purees, but she just stares at me like I’ve got a plate of something weird. It’s so frustrating!      I remember that phase. It felt like she was testing me every time. But you’ll get there – it’s just a matter of time and patience. And don’t worry, the nursery is going to be so good for her. You know what I mean?      Yeah, I do. I just hope I’ll be able to cope with the time apart. I mean, I’m not sure how I’ll manage without her crying in the middle of the night. I’ve been so used to her being close.      I know, it’s all very new. But think about what you’ll gain from it. You’ll get some time for yourself, and you’ll be able to go back to work with a clearer head. Plus, the baby will be getting more social interaction. I think it’ll be good for both of you.      I hope so. I just need to get through the next few weeks. And maybe I’ll take a short trip somewhere – like the Lake District? I think it would help me reset.      That sounds lovely. You deserve a break. And maybe we can plan a family holiday once the baby is a bit more settled. That’d be something to look forward to.      Yeah, I’d like that. It’s going to be a bit of a rollercoaster, but I think we’ll make it through.

So, I just got a call from the police saying they want a statement about that incident last weekend. I’m still trying to wrap my head around it. I mean, what exactly happened? I was just at the café, you know, as usual.      Yeah, I heard. It’s one of those things that you think is all in your head. You’re just having a quiet cup of tea, and then suddenly, you're being hauled in for a statement. What’s the full story, really?      I saw the news about it. They said there was a dispute over a parking space, and someone got a bit too heated. But honestly, I don’t see how that’s a police matter. I mean, who even calls the police over a parking argument?      Oh, it doesn’t have to be a big thing. They just want to cover all bases, you know. Anyway, I’m not sure if they’ll even need a statement. But I guess it’s better to be safe than sorry. Although, I’m still not sure what the fuss is about. I mean, we’ve all had a bit of a row over parking. It’s not like we’re in a war.      You’d think. But I’ve got this phone bill from EE that’s just gone up again. I don’t even know what they’re charging me for. Oh, and I’m supposed to be giving a statement to the police by next week—what’s the point? It’s like they want to make a mountain out of a molehill.      I know what you mean. I’m still waiting for my tax return. It’s been weeks. I’m trying to plan the week, but every time I try, something comes up. And I’ve got that meeting with the council about the new health and safety regulations. I’m going to have to take time off work for that.      Yeah, I feel you. I’ve been trying to plan a weekend trip with my sister, but the store’s been so busy, I can’t even get a day off. I go in on my day off, and then I’m so tired I can’t even enjoy the weekend. I’m thinking of taking a break next week, just to recharge.      You should. I’m going to take a weekend away myself.

So, I heard you mentioned Spartacus the other day. I’ve been trying to get around to watching it, but I keep putting it off. I’m more of a history buff, so I thought I’d see how accurate it is. You know, I mean, the gladiators—Deianira’s story, the whole  Hannibal  thing, that’s all Roman history, isn’t it?      Yeah, I mean, it’s not entirely accurate, but it’s a good dramatization. You know, I watched the first few episodes when I was in Cyprus. My mum used to talk about the Roman occupation of Cyprus, and I thought it’d be cool to see how they portrayed it. My uncle even said he saw a gladiator in a local market when he was a kid, but I don’t know if that’s true.      Ha, that sounds like something out of a novel. I’ve been thinking about Roman history in general lately. I even got a mortar and pestle to grind spices, so I could cook like the Romans did—though I haven’t gotten around to making that bread yet. I mean, the bread they ate was different, right? They used flour, water, and something else, maybe wheat?      Yeah, they used wheat, but also barley. And they had these really advanced baking techniques. I’m trying to make my own bread now, but I’ve been using a sourdough starter. It’s kind of like the Romans’ method, but with a modern twist.      That’s interesting. I’d love to see how you do it. Anyway, I was thinking about your grandmother’s garden the other day. She used to grow a lot of herbs and spices, like oregano and thyme. Maybe that’s where you got your interest in herbs and spices from.      Yeah, she always said she’d be a Roman if she wasn’t born in England. She’s got these old jars full of dried herbs, and she insists I use them in my cooking. I’ve even started using them in my tea.      That’s cool. I’ve been trying to make my own teas, too. I’ve got a few different blends, some with cinnamon and cardamom, others with mint and lemon. I even bought some chickpeas from the market down the road, thinking about making hummus.      I’ve got a bag of chickpeas in the fridge, too.

Right, so the English test was yesterday, wasn’t it? I was so nervous, I think I forgot half the vocabulary.      Yeah, I know, I felt the same. I was doing so well in the reading section, but then the writing part—oh my god, I couldn’t even start.      Me too! I tried to write about the seaside, but I just couldn’t get the right words out. I mean, I know the words, but when it comes to putting them together in a proper paragraph, it’s like a different language.      It’s so frustrating! I thought I was doing okay in the lessons, but when it actually matters, I’m like a complete blank. I swear, the teacher is like a robot, just repeating the same things over and over. I wish she’d stop talking about "descriptive language" and just give us some real examples.      Haha, yeah, I get that. I remember one time, she showed us a paragraph about the wind-band, and it was so over the top, like “the wind blew passionately across the orchestra, creating a symphony of emotion.” I mean, who talks like that in real life?      Exactly! I mean, we’re supposed to be writing about our school, our art lessons, our French class, the people we see in the corridors—like, what’s the point of all that fancy writing? I’d rather just write what actually happened.      I know, right? But I guess it’s all about getting the marks. I mean, I still got an A, so maybe I’m not as bad as I thought.      Yeah, but I still got a C. I can’t believe it. I thought I was doing better. I mean, I even joined the wind-band. My brother plays the flute, and he said I could try it too.      Oh, you did? That’s cool! I tried once, but I couldn’t even hold the flute properly. I think I panicked and dropped it.      Haha, that sounds like you. I think you’re more of a drawing person. I mean, you’re always drawing in your notebook during English lessons.      Yeah, I guess I am. I mean, the art teacher said I’ve got a real eye for detail. I even drew a picture of the wind-band yesterday.      Oh, really? Show it to me sometime. I’d love to see it.

You know, I still can’t get over how different the accents are in this part of the country. It’s like every town has its own dialect. I was in Newcastle the other day, and that  Yorkshire  twang—oh, it was so strong. I couldn’t understand a word the first time someone said “bairn” instead of “child.”      Yeah, I mean, it’s part of the culture. We’ve got our own way of speaking. It’s not just the accent, it’s the way we talk about things. Like, “How’s the missus?” instead of “How’s your wife?” My gran still says “bairn” like it’s the most natural thing in the world.      That’s the thing, isn’t it? I remember when I was a teacher, I used to get confused with the students. Some came from Newcastle, some from Hull, and others from Darlington. They all had different ways of speaking. I even had to get a grammar book just to understand half of what they were saying. It was like a whole other language!      I remember when I was teaching in Hull too – it was a bit of a shock. I had to learn to say “lorry” instead of “truck” and “biscuit” instead of “cookie.” It made me realize how much language is tied to place. Even the way people talk about food is different. In Yorkshire, they call a “scone” a “biscuit,” and in Darlington, I guess it’s just a scone.      And the football? You can’t talk about sports without mentioning the local team. I used to root for Newcastle United, but now I just watch the games. It’s hard to keep up with all the rivalries. My mate’s dad used to say, “If you don’t support Newcastle, you’re not from here.”      That’s true. Sport is such a big part of the community. I remember when I lived in Manchester, you could tell where someone was from just by the team they supported. It’s the same here – you don’t get much more local than that.      You know what I’m thinking? We should have a big family get-together sometime. Maybe next month? It’s been too long since we’ve all been together. I’d love to hear more about your travels – you’ve been to some places I’ve never even heard of.

So, I was telling my dad earlier that I think my genes are to blame for my weight. I mean, I’ve tried everything—running, dieting, even those ridiculous gym memberships. But no matter how hard I try, I just can’t seem to lose the last few pounds. I think it’s in my DNA.      Yeah, I can see that. My wife’s got the same thing. She’s always been a big girl, and no matter what she does, she just can’t seem to shed the weight. I think it’s in the family. My mum was like that too—always had a bit of a tummy, even when she was fit as a fiddle.      I’m not sure about genes. I think it’s more about the food. I mean, I’ve always been lazy with eating. When I was a kid, my mum would make me eat all this healthy stuff, and I’d just throw it away. I’d rather have chips and a bit of cake. I think it’s the way we were brought up.      That’s probably part of it. I’ve read a few studies that say environment plays a huge role. You’re more likely to be obese if your family eats that way, or if you grow up in an area where there’s not much access to fresh food.      There’s also this thing about people being sedentary. Like, I used to work in an office, and even though I’d walk a bit, I’d still be sitting most of the day. Now I’m a lecturer, and I’m actually more active. I lecture a lot, and I have to stand up and move around.      Yeah, I think that’s true. My job’s pretty physical—I fix cars. I’m on my feet all day, and I’ve got to lift things. So I’m not sitting around all day like some people. But I still eat too much. I mean, I can’t help it.      I think that’s the problem with us oldies. We just don’t care as much about dieting anymore. We’ve had our fill of trying to look good.      You know what’s funny is that obesity is becoming more common, but I think it’s not just about genes or environment—it’s also about money. Like, if you’re on a low income, you can’t afford fresh fruit and vegetables.

So, I just got an email from the department head about Moodle. I think it's time we started integrating it more into our courses. Have you seen the latest update?      Yeah, I saw it. It's pretty comprehensive, but I’m still a bit overwhelmed. I mean, it’s all about making everything digital, right? I get that it’s efficient, but I worry about the learning curve. A lot of our students are used to just using Blackboard, and now we're switching to Moodle.      I know what you mean. It's not just about the software—it’s about how we structure our content. I’ve been looking at the templates, and they’re actually quite flexible. My lectures are all online now, so I think Moodle is going to help streamline the process. You know, it's not just about uploading materials—it’s about making sure the interface is user-friendly for both us and the students.      That makes sense. I guess the key is to figure out what works best for each module. I’ve been trying to set up a module for my Digital Media course, and it's been a bit of a struggle. I’ve spent the last two evenings setting up the quiz section, and it’s still not quite where I want it.      I can relate. I spent last night trying to get the assignment submission feature working properly. It took me ages to figure out how to set up the due dates and feedback options. But once you get the hang of it, it’s actually pretty intuitive.      I guess it’s just a matter of time. I think the more we use it, the more comfortable we’ll get. I also think it's worth investing a bit of time to do some training or maybe watch some tutorials. I’ve found some YouTube videos that are really helpful.      Definitely. I found a couple of webinars that the university put together. They walk you through the basics, and they even have a support forum where you can ask questions. It’s a bit of a learning curve, but it's not insurmountable.      Yeah, I think I’ll try that. I mean, it's part of the job, right? We’re both lecturers, and it’s our responsibility to adapt. Plus, Moodle has some really cool features—like the ability to track student engagement and provide real-time feedback.

I can't believe how much I'm still affected by the jet lag. I swear, I've been up since dawn and I'm still half-asleep.      You’re not the only one. I woke up at 5 this morning and just couldn't get back to sleep. I think it's the baby's sleep schedule that's messing with us.      Yeah, I know. She's been up every two hours, like clockwork. It's like she's trying to teach us how to be nocturnal.      I can't even imagine. I mean, I've had some late nights, but nothing like this. I feel like I'm living in a different time zone every time I try to sleep.      I know. It's so frustrating. But at least we’re getting to know each other better. I mean, I used to think I was the one who stayed up late, but now I'm the one who's actually awake at 3 a.m.      I think we're both in the same boat. It’s like we’re learning the ropes of parenthood together. But I can’t wait for her to start sleeping through the night.      Me too. I’ve been trying to make the most of these late nights. I’ve been reading some books about child development and even writing a little in my journal. It’s weird how much you start to think about everything.      Yeah, it's like your brain is constantly recalibrating. I’ve been trying to get back into my old habit of going to the theatre. I miss the local dramatic performance we had last month. It was absolutely brilliant.      I know. I still can't believe how much I enjoyed that. It was so emotional, and the set design was incredible. I think I'm going to try to get tickets for the next one. I need something to take my mind off the baby.      That’s a good idea. We could go together. It would be nice to have a little date night without worrying about the baby.      That sounds perfect. I’ll check if there are any seats left. I’m sure the tickets are going to be harder to come by now that the baby’s due.      Yeah, I can imagine. But I think we’ll manage. We’ve got each other, and we’ve got the baby.

So, I was just thinkin’... I’ve been havin’ a right chatty time with some old friends from back in Germany. You know, those blokes who ended up in Libya, or in Syria. It’s funny how life turns out, isn't it? Some of ‘em are still out there, tryin’ to make a go of it, while others have moved on.      Yeah, it’s always interesting how people end up in different places. My cousin’s been in Iraq for a while now. He’s an interpreter, like me. But the politics there... it’s a mess. The oil money, the Wahabi influence – it’s like a nightmare.      I know, I know. I’ve read a few articles about that. It’s a bit of a paradox, isn’t it? You have these regions that are rich in oil, but people are still starvin’ and sufferin’. I mean, what’s the point of all that wealth if it’s not being used for the people?      Absolutely. And it’s not just about the money. There’s this whole ideological stuff – the Wahabi movement, the extremists. It’s like they’re trying to impose their own version of what Islam should be, and it’s causing a lot of conflict. I’ve seen how it affects young people. They’re confused, torn between their culture and what’s being pushed on them.      I can imagine. I've had a few students from there. They all have such mixed feelings. Some of them are trying to fit in, others are trying to hold on to their roots. It’s a tough spot to be in. But I suppose that’s the nature of being young and trying to find your way in the world.      Yeah, I guess that’s the case. It’s funny how that plays out. I’ve also been thinking about getting a new visa – I’ve got this friend who’s helping me set it up. It’s a bit of a hassle, but it’s necessary. I mean, I can’t work here without it, and I’ve got a family to support.      I know how that feels. I’ve been thinkin’ about movin’ house myself. The old place is gettin’ a bit too small for me and the boys. I’m lookin’ for somethin’ a bit more central, closer to the university. You ever think about movin’?

So, I just wanted to say, the roast lamb was absolutely divine. I think it was the perfect balance of crispy skin and juicy meat. You really outdid yourself, Speck.      Thank you, Elise. I’ve been practicing my roasting technique since I was a boy. Got it from my mum, honestly. She used to make the best roast dinners. Although, I have to say, I think the TV in the dining room might be a bit much. It’s so loud, and it’s hard to hear the conversation.      Oh, don’t say that, love. That TV is a real gem. I remember when I was teaching at the school, I used to bring my students here for a break. It was a bit of a haul, but the view from the window and the TV made it worth it. Plus, it’s got that Scottish tablet thing going on — the one that’s been in the family for generations. It’s got a bit of a crack, but it still works.      Oh, the tablet! I still can’t believe you managed to get it fixed. I mean, it looked like it was going to be a lost cause. And the stories that come with it — I mean, it’s practically a family heirloom.      Exactly. I got it from my aunt, who had it since the 50s. It’s got all these old phone numbers and handwritten notes. You can almost hear the voices of the people who used it. It’s a bit of a treasure, really. Though, I must say, I’m still not sure about that cruise you mentioned. I mean, going on a cruise with all those people? Sounds a bit like being in a fishbowl.      Oh, come on, Ron. You’ve always been the adventurous type. I remember when you tried skydiving for the first time. You thought it was like jumping out of a plane and landing on a mattress. And yet here you are, grumbling about a cruise.      I’m just realistic. I mean, I’ve got to take care of the dogs, and I’ve got this rental place. I’m not going to be running off to a cruise with a bunch of strangers. I’d go mad. Plus, I’ve been trying to get into a workout routine. I started going to the gym three times a week, and it’s already making a difference.

Right, so I was thinking, we need to get our heads together about food. I’m sick of just popping out to the shop and grabbing whatever’s on sale. It’s not like we don’t have the money or the time, but it’s just not right. I mean, I saw this place down the road that sells proper meals, like real food, not just chips and beans. You should come with me.      Oh, yeah, I’d love to. But I was just thinking the same thing. I mean, I’ve been surviving on toast and tea for weeks. I’m starting to think I’m going to turn into a human version of a bird that just eats seeds. You know what I mean?      You're not the only one. I’ve been living off takeaways and cereal. My flatmate’s been trying to convince me to cook, but I’m just not in the mood. I’m too busy studying, and I don’t have the skills. I mean, I can boil an egg, but that’s about it.      You’re all missing the point. We need to start cooking together. It’s not just about food; it’s about building something. I remember when I first started teaching, I was so worried about getting the lesson right, but once I got into the rhythm, it all started to make sense. Same with cooking. Once you get the hang of it, it’s not that hard. And besides, it’ll be a bonding experience.      Yeah, I guess you’re right. I mean, we’ve got the ingredients. I’ve got the kettle. I’ve got the saucepan. What we need is a plan. Maybe we could take turns cooking each week. One meal a day, just to keep things interesting.      That sounds doable. But I’m not sure about the logistics. Like, who’s going to do the shopping? I don’t want to be the one who’s always running out of something.      That’s a good point. Maybe we should all agree on a list of essentials. Like, we can all chip in for the basics—flour, rice, pasta, sauce. Then, once we’ve got that covered, we can go for the fancy stuff.      And if we ever run out of something, we just order a takeaway. It’s not like we’re aiming for Per Se or anything.

So, I’ve been thinking about what we need to do for Mum’s lesson. I got the recipe for the Victoria sponge, and I thought we could make that.      Yaaay! I love cake! Can we put sprinkles on it?      Yeah, me too! I like making things with my hands.      Of course you can. We’ll have to get the flour and butter and eggs. Oh, and the vanilla extract. Do you remember where we saw the vanilla extract?      I think it was in the fridge in the kitchen.      Or maybe in the pantry? I saw it there last week.      Well, we’ll have to check both. I’m just trying to remember what the recipe said. It said, “Preheat the oven to 180°C,” so we’ll need to set that.      Can I put the cake in the oven?      Only if you promise not to touch it when it’s glowing. It’s hot, you know.      I’m not a baby!      No, but your hands are still tiny. You can help with the mixing though. Just don’t lick the spoon.      I won’t! I’ve got a clean mouth!      She does!      Anyway, we also need to think about the lesson. I was thinking of doing a baking lesson for the class, like how to make a basic cake.      Can we do something with chocolate?      Maybe a chocolate fondant? It’s a bit more advanced, but it’s fun. I think it would be a hit.      Is it like a cake?      It’s more like a little chocolate ball. You melt the chocolate and pour it into a tin, then put it in the oven. It’s really cute.      I want to make that!      Me too!      Well, we’ll have to get the chocolate, butter, and egg. Oh, and the tin. I think we have one in the cupboard.      Over there! I saw it last week.      Thanks, love. I think that’s all for now. We can start baking tomorrow.      Can we start today?      Maybe tomorrow. It’s not a half birthday celebration today. We need to save it for tomorrow.      Okay! I can’t wait!      Me neither!      I know you can’t wait. I can’t wait either. Let’s get the ingredients.      I’ll go get the flour!      I’ll get the butter!      Alright, you two are a team. I’ll get the eggs.      We’re going to make a cake!

You know, I was just thinking about that new car I saw the other day—this electric one from a startup in Norwich. It’s got this super sleek design, and the tech inside is just… wow. I mean, it’s got a touchscreen bigger than my laptop, and it can update itself over the internet. I reckon it’s the future of driving, but I’ve got to admit, I’m still a bit nervous about not having a traditional engine.      Yeah, I saw that too. It’s like they’ve taken everything we love about cars and flipped it on its head. But honestly, I think there’s something to be said for the old school stuff. I still prefer the sound of a real engine, you know? There’s a kind of soul to it. But I’ll be the first to admit, when it comes to tech, I’m behind the curve.      You say that, but I’ve seen the way you use your phone. It’s like you’ve got the internet in your hand. I still struggle with Facebook, honestly. I’ve got this account, but I can’t seem to figure out how to unfollow someone without looking like a total tech failure. My brother-in-law showed me how, but I still end up accidentally liking something I didn’t mean to.      Oh, I’ve been there. It’s like learning to ride a bike—once you get the hang of it, it’s second nature. I remember the first time I used a smart speaker. I said, “Hey Google, play some music,” and it started playing a lecture on quantum physics. I was so confused, I thought I had finally gone mad.      That’s barely even funny. I once tried to use my phone to order a takeaway and ended up ordering a whole set of cookbooks. The app thought I was a bookworm, not a hungry person.      We’re all just trying to keep up, aren’t we? It’s like we’re in a race to see who can adapt the fastest. Still, I think it’s good that we’re all learning. I mean, without the internet, how would we even know about this electric car? Probably wouldn’t have seen it unless someone posted a picture on Facebook.      Touché. I guess we’re all just digital pioneers, one messy Facebook post at a time.

So, I'm telling you, I've had one of the worst days ever. I got stuck in the rain on the way to work, my phone died, and then I had to wait for like half an hour for a customer to finish their coffee. Just...  aggravating .      You’re always complaining about work, aren’t you? You’ve only been a part-time sales assistant for a month.      Hey, I'm just being real. It’s not like I get paid well or anything. I mean, I guess it's better than nothing, but it's not like I'm making a fortune or anything.      Yeah, you’re just being dramatic. I mean, you're a student too. You could be studying for your degree, not flipping burgers.      Well, I'm trying to make ends meet, you know? I'm not on benefits or anything. I have to work to help out with the bills.      Yeah, I get that. But you’ve got to remember, you’re not the only one in this country who’s got work. I mean, I'm doing okay too – just trying to finish my undergrad, and I barely have time to breathe.      Right, right. I’m just saying, I’m not complaining about the work itself. I mean, it’s not that bad. It's just the customers sometimes. I had this guy today who kept asking me if I worked in a ‘sushi bar,’ and I’m like, “No, I work at a coffee shop.”      Classic. I remember when I was your age, I used to get confused by things too. Like that film we watched earlier –  Cloudy with a Chance of Meatballs  – did you get the hidden meaning?      I dunno. I thought it was just a kids’ movie about food. But I guess there’s always some deeper meaning, right? Like, maybe the world is going to be overrun by food, or something.      Yeah, that’s what I thought too. Maybe it’s about capitalism and how we’re all just food in a box, or something.      Okay, that’s a bit too deep for me. I think I’m just gonna stick to the surface meaning for now.      You’re missing out. I think it's also about the importance of family and community, like how the town comes together in the end. Or maybe even a metaphor for the real world being a little too much, and we all just want to be in a place where everything is soft and sweet.

So, you're a taxi driver? I thought you’d be more of a football fan, like the rest of us in this part of the world.      Aye, I do my bit for the game, mate. I’ve been driving for over twenty years, and I’ve picked up more than just fares. I’ve seen every major team come and go. But I’ve never been one for the politics stuff, to be honest. Unless it's about who's gonna be in charge of the local council and how that affects the football clubs.      I couldn’t agree more. Politics has always been a bit of a minefield for me. My lectures are all about literature and language, not the kind you’d find in the news. But I suppose it's unavoidable. The government's always playing with the rules, isn’t it? Especially after New Labour—Tony Blair and all that. They did some pretty controversial stuff back then.      Yeah, I remember that. I was just starting out as a driver, and I used to listen to the radio every morning. Blair was all about the "third way", wasn’t he? Tryin' to be the middle ground between the left and the right. But I always thought it was a bit of a gimmick. You can’t really be the middle ground in a world that’s divided as much as ours.      Precisely. And now we're in a different era. The government's more divided than ever. You can't ignore the impact it's having on people's lives—especially when it comes to things like the economy and social services. It's like every time you turn around, there's another policy that changes the game.      I know what you mean. I've seen the changes in my own little world. The councils are under more pressure, and that's affecting the way the local clubs operate. I think it's a bit of a shame, really. Football’s a game that brings people together. You can talk about politics all you want, but when the match is on, it’s the only thing that matters.      Yeah, I couldn't disagree more. Football is a great leveller. You don’t have to agree on politics to be able to enjoy a match. And what's more, you don’t have to be a politician to understand the importance of unity.

So, I was sorting through some old BNC recordings last night, and I found this one from the 90s. It’s got this really  interesting  accent, like a mix of East Anglia and somewhere else… I mean, it's  so  different from what we hear now.      Yeah, I remember those. They were a bit weird, weren't they? I mean, I got into BNC because of my job—every editor should know how people used to speak. But honestly, it’s kind of fascinating how much language has changed. You know, even in the way people talk about social media now.      Exactly! I was just thinking about how people use phrases like “linked in” or “swipe right” now. It’s like a whole new lexicon. I’ve been working on a project about how language evolves through social media. It’s wild.      Oh, really? What’s the focus?      Well, I’m looking at how people use short forms and slang in their professional contexts. It’s not just kids anymore—everybody’s using it. Even in LinkedIn posts. I mean, I saw one yesterday where someone said, “Just dropped some knowledge on the team,” and I’m like…  what?       That’s not even slang—it’s just a bad attempt at being cool. But seriously, I think it’s just part of how we communicate with our phones now. We’re used to typing fast and not having to speak properly.      I agree. And you know, it’s different depending on where you’re from. My sister’s in Spain, and she told me she’s starting to use some Spanish phrases in her English. Like “¡Qué bien!” or “¡Vale!” She says it makes her sound more  connected  to the culture.      That’s cute. I’ve been thinking about doing a trip to Wales with my cousin. It’s been a while since I’ve visited. The last time, I got lost in Abergavenny and accidentally ended up in a pond. I still don’t know how that happened.      You’re not the first. I went to the Maldives with my brother, and he got scared of flying. He kept saying, “I don’t want to die in the ocean!” But he survived, obviously.      I’d be terrified of flying too. I mean, I can’t even get on a plane without checking the weather forecast and the route. It’s just so  aircraft —not to be rude, but I think I’d rather go to the Whales.

So, I’ve been thinking about getting a tattoo for ages, but I just can’t decide what to get. You know, like, something meaningful but not too obvious.      That’s the thing, isn’t it? You want it to mean something, but you don’t want it to be like, “Oh, that’s just a standard thing.” I’ve got a little ink on my wrist from my twenties, but I’d probably go back and change it if I could.      Yeah, I mean, I’ve been to a few tattoo places, but I keep putting it off. I’m still not sure if I’m ready for the commitment. You know, like, it’s not like a piercing or something you can just take off.      No, it’s a bit of a life decision. But I think once you get one, you start to see the point. Like, you’re putting something permanent on your body that represents something important to you.      I guess. I’m just worried about what people might think. Like, if I get something too weird or too… I don’t know, maybe too dark.      I get that. But it’s your body, right? You should do what makes you happy. Although, if you're going to get one, maybe wait until you’re in a better place in life. Like, maybe not when you're just starting out.      So, what’s being discussed?      Oh, just tattoos. We were talking about getting one.      Yeah, he’s been thinking about it. But it’s a bit of a big decision.      I get it. I had one when I was younger, but it was just a little symbol I liked. I think it’s a good idea. As long as you’re happy with it, it’s fine.      You got one?      Yeah, I got a small one on my arm – just a simple design. It’s not too flashy. But it’s something that reminds me of a time in my life.      That’s the idea, right? You don’t need to be over the top. Just something personal.      I guess. Maybe I’ll just do something small. Like, maybe a symbol or something.      That’s a good start. And if you change your mind, you can always get another one.      Yeah, just don’t end up with a tattoo that you regret.      I’ll keep that in mind.

So, I just got this pair of leather boots from a vintage shop in Brixton. They’re like... mid-70s, I think. They’re really comfortable, but the soles are a bit worn. I’m trying to decide if I should get them resoled or just replace them.      Oh, I got some really good ones too, actually. I found them on a market stall in Manchester. They’re made in Italy, I think. Oh, and they were only £30. You can’t beat that. But I’ve had them for a few months now and they’re still holding up.      That’s great! I’ve always been a bit of a shoe snob, I guess. I like to think I can tell the difference between a good quality boot and a cheap one. I mean, the leather just feels different in your hand.      I know what you mean. I used to work in a store that sold designer shoes, and I got pretty good at identifying the materials. But honestly, I’ve noticed that a lot of the cheaper brands are copying the same styles now. It’s kind of a shame, because you end up paying a premium for something that’s not really different.      That’s so true. I think it’s mostly because of the fashion trends these days. Everyone’s after the same look, so the manufacturers just start churning them out. I remember when I was younger, you could find more unique designs.      Yeah, I remember that too. I think it’s also because of the internet. Everything’s so accessible now. Even if you don’t have a lot of money, you can find something that looks good. Although, I do think the quality is still an issue. I’ve bought some really cheap boots that fell apart after a week.      That’s a good point. I’ve been thinking about getting into some running shoes that are more supportive. I’ve been going to a yoga class twice a week, and I’ve noticed my feet are aching more.      That’s a good idea. I’ve been thinking about starting some exercise classes too. I’ve been trying to get into swimming, but I’m not the most confident in the water. Maybe I’ll start with some Pilates or something.      Pilates is a good one. I’ve been doing it for a few months now, and it really helps with core strength.

So, I was just thinking about how we both had that one friend in uni who had the most ridiculous toe nails. You remember Tom? The guy who wore socks with sandals and had a whole collection of glittery toe caps?      Oh, I remember Tom! He was  so  into his look. I swear he thought he was in a boy band. You should have seen him in the chemistry lab—wearing those neon yellow toe caps, and he was supposed to be mixing some kind of acid. It was  so  not the image you want when you're trying to avoid a lab accident.      Yeah, I think he got caught with a glowing solution in his shoe once. The lab tech nearly had a heart attack. And then he got banned from the lab for a month. I still remember the look on his face when he came back—like he’d been exiled from a religion or something.      He definitely had a bit of a cult following, though. I mean, he had that whole aesthetic going on. You know, that sort of "I’m from the future" vibe.      He  was  from the future. Or at least, he thought he was. I think he still believes he’s a prophet of some sort. He was telling me once that he was getting messages from the universe through his toe nails.      Sounds like he was trying to live a bit of a  divine  life. Though, honestly, I think he just wanted to be noticed. I mean, he was a lecturer, right? I mean, he was a lecturer in “Alternative Sciences” or something like that.      Oh, I remember that. He was teaching something like “The Philosophy of Glitter and the Enigma of Toe Nails.” It was  so  niche. I think he was trying to get a grant for a study on the psychological effects of toe cap color on human behavior.      I can just imagine the funding panel—like, “We’re giving this guy a grant to study toe nails? That’s it?” But he was  so  passionate about it. And I think he actually believed in it.      Yeah, and we used to joke that he was the only person in the world who could get a grant for something like that. It was both ridiculous and beautiful in its own way.      I think he’d still be doing it if he wasn’t so old.

So, I heard you mentioned something about a new movie coming out. Which one was it again? I think it was that one with the conspiracy element, like the ones we used to love back in the day.      Yeah, that’s the one— The Truth About the Moon Landing . Got to say, it’s pretty wild. I mean, I know it’s just a film, but it’s making me wonder if there’s more to the story than we’ve been told. You ever think about that stuff?      Honestly, I do. I mean, I’m a language teacher, so I’ve always been interested in how stories are told and how people interpret them. But I’ve got to admit, the conspiracy theories around the moon landing are just too good to ignore. I mean, the whole thing about the flags waving in a vacuum? That’s just nuts.      Exactly! And I still can’t believe that some people are still convinced it was all a hoax. It’s not like we have any proof, but the film makes it seem plausible. I mean, I get it—people want to believe in bigger truths. I think that’s what drives conspiracy theories. It’s like a way to feel like you’re part of something bigger.      That’s a good point. I remember when I was younger, I used to watch all these documentaries about the government covering things up. It got me thinking about how much we don’t know. Still, I think it’s important to stay grounded in reality. Although, I won’t lie, it’s fun to speculate occasionally.      I agree. I think the key is to stay curious but not let it consume you. Speaking of which, I heard you’re planning to travel to Spain for that language course you mentioned. How’s that going?      It’s going well, actually. I’m excited. My Spanish is still basic, but I’m improving every day. And the people there are so friendly. I think I’ll be able to pick up a few more phrases before I head back. We’ll see how that goes.      That’s great. You always did have a knack for languages. I still remember when you taught me how to say “I love you” in French. It was one of those moments that made me realize how much I could learn from you.

Dad, remember when we used to read  Jamaica Inn  together? That book got us so scared we had to stop reading it in the car. I still think about that haunted inn every time we pass a lonely house on the road.      I remember that! You were so scared you started humming the  Wizard of Oz  theme to calm yourself down. I couldn’t help but laugh, even though I was worried about you. You were always into those old books— Sherlock Holmes ,  Alice in Wonderland , even the fairy tales. You had a real love for stories, even back then.      Yeah, I guess that’s why I still love reading. I just finished  The Wind in the Willows  the other day, and it reminded me of how much I enjoyed those classic tales. I was thinking about how different it must have been back then, with telegrams and Morse code and all that. I mean, I never thought I’d be able to read a book and not have to worry about missing a call or something.      You’re not as technologically dependent as you think, lass. You still like to read, and that’s a good thing. You know, when I was your age, I used to read  The Railway Children  and  The Secret Garden  by the fire at night. I used to imagine all those stories were real.      That’s what I do. I like to imagine the world through the stories. Even the road we’re driving on now has its own kind of story. The way the colours change as we pass the hills, the way the flowers are blooming, the birds flying by—like it’s all part of some great tale.      You’ve got a vivid imagination. That’s why I always thought you’d make a good writer. You’ve got the kind of mind that can see something simple and turn it into something magical. I just hope you don’t get too lost in your imagination. We’ve got a long drive ahead, and we need to make sure we’re on the right path.      Don’t worry, I’ll keep my eyes on the road. And I’ll make sure I don’t miss the caravan park we’re stopping at tonight. Although, if I see a wind turbine, I might take a photo to remember it like one of those old books—just to keep the story alive.

So, I was just thinking about that time I tried to cheat at Monopoly. I got so obsessed with it, I started skimming the rules, like, “Oh, you can borrow money from the bank,” and then the next thing I know, I’m in a massive debt and I’m like,  “I’m not paying rent again!”       Aye, I remember that too. I used to play with my granddaughters, and it was always me who was the one losing. Didn’t matter how much money I had – they’d just keep buying properties and I’d be stuck with a hotel and the Bank of England.      I remember playing Monopoly with my dad when I was a kid. He was a bit of a cheater, too. He’d take the rent money and put it into his piggy bank. I used to think he was a genius.      He didn’t have a piggy bank, did he? He just kept the money. I remember being so mad.      Aye, and he’d say, “You’ll be rich one day – it’s all about strategy!”      I still think that’s the best way to teach kids about money. But somehow, he never taught me how to budget.      No, he just taught me how to lose money.      Aye, and now you’re a corpus administrator. That’s a  real  career!      Oh, it’s  so  glamorous. I just manage data and make sure people don’t put the wrong accent in the database.      Sounds like a steady job. I work as a consultant engineer, so I’m always on the move. I once had to meet a client in Birmingham and I got lost. It was like  Narnia  out there.      I remember when I was working for BT, I used to travel all over the country. I go to Wigan, Manchester, even as far as Liverpool. But now I just sit in the garden and watch the world go by.      I can’t imagine not working. I’d go nuts.      I’ve got a good job, but I think I’d rather be on holiday. I just got back from Channel swimming. It was so cold, I thought I was going to die.      Aye, you’d have to be mad to swim the Channel. I used to work on the railways and I could have done that. But I’d have been too scared of the water.

So, I’ve been thinking about that weaver fish I saw on the website. It’s like a hybrid between a goldfish and a betta, right? I think it’s called a “wels catfish” or something like that?      No, no, no. That’s the wels catfish. A weaver fish is a different creature altogether. It’s actually a type of fish that lives in coral reefs. They’re quite colorful, like little rainbow fish. You’d have to keep them in a big tank or a pond. You sure you want to go down that route?      I know, I know. But the idea of having something that’s not just a regular goldfish is tempting. Plus, I’ve been meaning to get a new fish tank anyway. But then again, moving house is on the horizon. I need to start thinking about this.      Yeah, moving house is on my mind too. I was just going to ask you—do you think we should start drawing up that item list? I’ve got a box with all the old to-do notes and stuff, but it’s getting a bit messy. I feel like we’re both scrambling a bit.      I was just thinking that too. I’ve been trying to remember everything I need to pack. I think I’ve got the big boxes sorted, but the small stuff—like chargers, plug sockets, and the like—is a nightmare. It’s one thing to pack your own things, but when it comes to the kitchen and bathroom, I feel like I’m missing key items.      Don’t worry, I’m sure we’ll get it sorted. Maybe we should start by listing the essentials. I mean, if we’re moving to Bedford, do you think we’ll need to buy a new set of dishes or can we just take what we’ve got?      Honestly, I’m not sure. We’ve got good stuff, but I also know that moving always comes with a bit of newness. I’ve been thinking about going to that local market near the station. They’ve got some good local produce. Maybe we can get a few basics there.      Sounds like a plan. I’ve got the list of what we need to bring. I just need to make sure we don’t leave anything out. And speaking of lists—do you think we should start tracking our travel plans too?

So, I was just thinking about that plant we bought last week. You know, the one with the bright yellow flowers. I’m telling you, it’s like it’s got a mind of its own. One day it’s thriving, the next it’s drooping like it’s been through a war.      Yeah, I remember. You said it was a “sun-loving” plant, and then you put it on the windowsill where the sun doesn’t even touch it. I mean, I got it for you, not for the plant. But honestly, it’s still hanging in there, isn’t it?      Yeah, and now you’re blaming me. I told you it needed more sun, and you said, “It’s got enough light, it’s not in the dark.” But then you move it to the kitchen, which is basically the darkest room in the house.      And now it’s getting a bit of sun from the laptop. I mean, it’s not like we’re giving it a full outdoor summer. But hey, I’m not the one who’s got a PhD and thinks they can grow plants like they’re doing research. You’re the one who was like, “It’s all about the soil pH, the water, and the light!”      Okay, okay, I’ll admit I might have overestimated my horticultural skills. But at least I know how to water it. You, on the other hand, just left it in the pot for weeks and then suddenly poured a whole bottle of water in at once.      I was trying to be efficient. You know what they say—less is more. Maybe I should start wearing that hairstyle you’re going for. The short, spiky one. It’s got that “I’ve got no time for maintenance” vibe.      Oh, you’d be a walking disaster. You’d end up with one side longer than the other and a split end that looks like a spider’s web.      I’ll take that as a compliment. Speaking of which, have you seen the new A-Level reforms? They’re making it harder than ever to get into uni. I mean, the NHS is struggling, the petrol crisis is making people go mad, and now we’ve got to take more exams?      Tell me about it. I’m so glad I’m not a student anymore. You’d go mad trying to keep up.

So, I was just telling my mates about the time I tried to smoke in the flat, and my roommate came in and nearly had a heart attack! I thought I was being super stealthy, but apparently, the smell spread like wildfire.      I bet that’s  not  the first time you’ve tried to hide it, is it? I mean, I remember you saying once that you wanted to be a “cool” student, but clearly, pulling out a cigarette in the middle of the night and pretending you're just getting a snack is  not  the way to go.      Yeah, I’ve seen you trying that before. You’re like a kid who thinks they’re sneaking candy into the house, but you end up getting caught with a bag of snacks and a pack of fags.      I knew you were up to something. And don’t even get me started on the fag smells in this flat. I swear, I could smell that stale smoke from the hallway, and I haven’t even seen you in a week.      Hey, I’ve been trying to quit! I just... I was stressed about uni. I mean, I’m in my third year, and I’ve got this essay due next week, and I don’t know if I can handle it. I’m already thinking about taking a gap year or something.      That sounds really heavy. I mean, I’m in the same boat. I’ve been thinking about being a feminist academic, but I’m scared I won’t be taken seriously. I mean, I’ve had a few professors who’ve treated me like I’m not  really  into it because I’m a woman.      Yeah, that’s the whole  feminism  thing, isn’t it? Like, you’re supposed to be strong, but then you’re told you’re not  qualified  enough to discuss it because you’re a woman.      I hear you. I’ve been trying to think about my future, too. I’m not sure if I want to do finance or work in the arts. I mean, I’m into design, but I’m not sure if that’s a real career path.      I’ve been thinking about it too. I’m really into social work, but I don’t know if I can afford to go into that. I mean, I’m not even sure if I can afford to live in Leeds anymore.

So, I just wanted to say, I think I need to start phasing out some of my friends. It’s not that I don’t like them, it’s just... I don’t know. I feel like I’m not really connecting with them the way I used to. It’s getting a bit exhausting, y’know?      Oh, really? That’s interesting. I mean, I can totally see how that could happen. I’ve had a few friends who just... drifted away over the years. It’s one of those things, isn’t it? You just kind of lose touch. But how do you even go about it? Do you just stop talking to them?      It’s not that simple, honestly. I’ve tried to talk to them, but it feels like they’re not really interested in what I’m saying anymore. Sometimes I’ll text them, and they’ll reply with a “later” or something, and I just... I don’t know. It makes me feel like I’m not important to them anymore. And that stings, you know?      Yeah, I know what you mean. I had this friend who used to be like family, but when life got hectic, we just... didn’t have time for each other. It was sad, but I think it was inevitable. But I guess the trick is to do it gently, right? You don’t want to burn bridges.      Exactly. I don’t want to be the one to just walk away. But I also don’t want to keep pretending everything’s fine when it’s not. I mean, is there a way to let them know you’re not as interested without being too harsh?      I think maybe you can start by just talking about it. Like, let them know you’re not as close as you used to be, and it’s not about them—it’s just... you’ve grown apart. Sometimes people get confused if you just stop showing up. They might think you’re angry or something.      That makes sense. I’ve been thinking about that. Maybe I can just say something like, “I really value our friendship, but I think we’ve both changed a lot over the years, and I’m not sure if we’re on the same page anymore.” I think that’s honest, but not too confrontational.      Yeah, that sounds good. You’re not being rude, you’re just being realistic.

So, I’ve been thinking about uni days, you know? I can’t believe it’s been nearly five years since I left. Still can’t get over how much I missed that café by the library. Remember when we used to study there?      Oh, I remember. You used to sit with that mug of tea that never seemed to go cold. I always thought you were gonna burn your tongue one day. Still, it was a great spot—quiet, peaceful. You used to write so much then. Didn’t you want to be a writer?      Yeah, I did. I thought I had the makings of something. But then I realized I preferred the idea of being a writer more than the actual work. Still, it taught me a lot. I mean, the way you can take a scene and twist it into something else. I’ve been trying to use that in my current project.      That’s good. You always had a way with words. I still get letters from you—sometimes, I think you’ve written more in the past year than in the last five. It’s like you’re always on the edge of something.      Yeah, I guess I am. I’ve been thinking about going back to university for a bit. Not full-time, but taking some courses here and there. Maybe in art? I mean, I never really got to study it beyond my A-levels. You know, I’ve been looking at a few exhibitions in the area. The one at the gallery on Hampstead Road was amazing—so much emotion in every piece.      That’s good. You’ve always had an eye for what moves you. I know that feeling. I used to walk past the galleries in Vienna every day. One time, I just stopped and looked at a painting for hours. It wasn’t even a famous one. I was just… struck by it.      That’s incredible. I’ve never been to Vienna, but I’ve always wanted to. I’ve been looking up travel plans. Maybe next year?      That’s a good idea. You should see the city. It’s so beautiful, and the art scene is second to none. I used to paint there sometimes. You’d love it. The people are friendly, and the food—oh, the food! You’d never get that sort of cuisine in London.

So, I just thought of something – do you ever feel like we’re the only ones who still think about eating  before  the gym? I mean, isn’t that like a superstition or something?      Not a superstition, more like a British tradition. You know, "breakfast is the most important meal of the day," and then you feel guilty if you skip it. Plus, I’ve always found that if you don’t eat before the gym, you end up rushing into a workout without energy, and then you feel like you’re cheating on your body or something.      Exactly! It’s like we’ve internalized this idea that you have to fuel your muscles first. I mean, I’m not even into the gym that much, but I still feel like I need to have a snack or something before I even get in the door. It’s weird, isn’t it? How we’ve incorporated that into our daily lives.      Yeah, and it’s not just about the gym, is it? I mean, even the way we talk about time—like, "I don’t have time to eat," or "I’m too busy." It’s like we’ve got this ingrained idea that time is something to be conquered, not something to be respected. You ever notice how we Brits are always saying things like, "I’ll get to it later," but then never do?      Oh, I know. I’ve heard that phrase so many times in my life. It’s like a British catchphrase. And it’s not just about time—it’s also about gender, isn’t it? I mean, being English is like having this complicated identity. You’re always trying to balance being modern and traditional, right?      Oh, absolutely. And it’s not just the gender stuff—it’s also about the silence. Like, we’re always expected to be polite, to not say anything too controversial. I’ve noticed that even in the gym, where you would think people are more open, there’s still this unspoken rule that you don’t talk about politics or religion.      Exactly. It’s weird, isn’t it? I’ve been thinking about it a lot lately. I mean, I’m semi-retired, so I go to the gym just to keep moving, not to work out. But even then, I feel like I need to act a certain way.

Well, I've been thinking about that hand-thrown mug I got from the market last week. You know the one with the daffodils on it?      Oh, I remember! You were so proud of it, even though it’s cracked on the handle. You told me it was “a true Yorkshire masterpiece.”      I know, I know. But it's still got character, don’t you think? You can’t buy that kind of charm in a shop, can you?      Not really. Though I do miss the real milk from the farm, you know. My knees are too stiff to go down to the shop these days.
